messages.content:
A 33-year-old male underwent a pre-employment medical checkup and was found to have an SGPT (ALT) level of 194. The patient reports that all other tests were normal, including: (1) CBC, (2) ESR and liver test(s), (3) urine routine, (4) blood group and Rh factor, (5) chest X-ray, (6) general physical examination, (7) fasting blood sugar and post-prandial blood sugar, (8) total cholesterol, (9) ECG, and (10) serum creatinine. The patient was advised to obtain a full-abdomen ultrasound, which was performed and was reported as normal except for mild fatty liver.

The patient also reports recent loose motions and took ofloxacin 200 mg with ornidazole 500 mg twice daily for 2 days (Oflox-OZ), then continued ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily for another 3 days due to cold and cough.

The patient asks what could be the reason for the elevated SGPT, whether the patient will obtain clearance for joining a new company, what should be done to lower SGPT levels, and what diet should be followed. The patient reports not being a heavy drinker and drinking only occasionally, and not being fond of junk food.
